- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-4.mdx`  _(via DatabaseLoader (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **16** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e0ce1b523c9cdb625211fc866593f57aee9223ee` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `344dfb668826d42ae886163477947fe1588170d4` — the merge of head `123588d87515bcb6c762cec4d1a0357d4d6d604f` into base `e0ce1b523c9cdb625211fc866593f57aee9223ee`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 344dfb668826d42ae886163477947fe1588170d4 && git checkout 344dfb668826d42ae886163477947fe1588170d4
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e0ce1b523c9cdb625211fc866593f57aee9223ee 123588d87515bcb6c762cec4d1a0357d4d6d604f && git checkout -B drift-repro e0ce1b523c9cdb625211fc866593f57aee9223ee && git merge --no-ff 123588d87515bcb6c762cec4d1a0357d4d6d604f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e0ce1b523c9cdb625211fc866593f57aee9223ee
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e0ce1b523c9cdb625211fc866593f57aee9223ee` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `df6d261521d40e4dc588ee9ec1befef8d605e2d8`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata/src/loaders/database-loader.ts, packages/metadata/src/package-slotted-store.ts + packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager-match-endpoint.test.ts, packages/metadata/src/loaders/database-loader.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-package-addressing.test.ts, docs/adr/0150 (D4)

### ① Derived judgments

- **Write side.** `slottedSaveTarget` now keys each stored row by `storeRowSlotKey(type, name, package, member)`, and `storeRowWriteKey` passes `slotIdentityOf(type, name, data)`. An action bound to an object therefore counts the holders of its `(object, name)`, as the in-memory `storeWriteKey` does, and never every package holding the name. For every other type (and object-less actions) `ownedIdentityOf` returns the bare name, so `storeRowSlotKey` reduces to `storeRowKey` and nothing moves. The unique-key bucket for `unnamed` stays per package (`storeRowKey(name, slotPackageOf(slot))`), which matches `sys_metadata`'s `(type, name, package_id, bundle_member)` key, so a write can never collide with another member's row.
- **Read side.** `loadManySlots` hands a package-less action row on, held for the one package binding the name to that row's object, only when all of these hold: the type is owner-keyed; the unscoped plural read kept the row under its own `[null, name]` key; it is the row the unscoped read keeps for that key (highest version); and exactly one package binds the `(object, name)`. The row is placed just before that package's own row of the object, so slot-first readers answer it, matching the store after the boot pass. Nothing is written back. I checked the one place this could drop a row: the holder is `storedItemPackageId(data)` when the row carries no package, but `readTypeRows` already sets `packageId` via `storedRowPackageId`, which falls back to the body. The holder row's slot key therefore matches the customization's key, and the customization is always consumed.
- **Red lines (ADR-0150).** One holder of the `(object, name)` keeps its behaviour (CONTROL pinned). Two holders of the same `(object, name)` still go to a package-less row (CONTROL pinned). Resolution is not loosened: the read side only aligns the no-pass read with what the pass already answers. The one outcome that moves for a single name-holder (BETA on `contact` alone; a package-less `account` save is now the environment's row, not BETA's) is the declared narrowing, and it removes a binding BETA never declared.
- **Changed pin.** `metadata-manager-match-endpoint.test.ts` moves from "row named o1 by the o2 save" to "left as stored". That is the right consequence of the per-`(object,name)` key: the o2 save no longer writes the package-less bucket. The follow-on object-less save names it first. Pinned.
- Coverage: six loader cases (each with its BEFORE), the no-pass and after-pass read agreement in both orders, a manager-register-plus-reboot round trip, and the runtime route judging and running one item over the stored rows in both save orders.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/metadata: patch` with `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, a BREAKING banner and the `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker: correct for a non-protocol narrowing (AGENTS.md). No stored row is rewritten. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds, since nothing an author writes is refused.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The changeset says no host in the workspace wires a `DatabaseLoader` for this path, so the narrowing reaches external hosts only (cloud). The ACCEPT should name that, and a cloud pin-bump note is owed.
- The "Not changed" paragraph is accurate: the boot pass's plural read still folds by name, and that half follows #32680's keyed-entry stamping. #32680's PR is #33299, which I reviewed at `fad580c0`. The two touch neighbouring helpers in `package-slotted-store.ts`. Re-read the merge result if #33299 lands first.
- CI at this head when read (16:59Z): 8 success, 16 skipped, 16 in progress, none red. The PR is still a draft. The ACCEPT re-reads every check at the landing head.

### ④ Design judgment

Seat ruling A on #32681 (ADR-0150 D4: a customization is keyed per `(object, name)`) requires the stored side to count holders exactly as the in-memory store does. Before this change the two disagreed, so the item in memory and the row after a reboot could name different holders. Reusing `slotIdentityOf` / `storeRowSlotKey`, instead of a second rule, keeps one definition of identity across both stores, and the reboot round-trip pin measures the agreement directly. Making the no-pass read hand the customization to its holder, without rebinding the row, is the minimal way to make reads independent of whether the pass ran, and it leaves migration to the D10 report. The design holds.
